claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

I can see you live in the UK and are asking about Child Benefit for Alex, who is 19 years old and lives with you.

Let me gather just a bit more information to make a proper assessment:

1. You mentioned Alex is 19 and in approved education - could you confirm that Alex is still in approved education or training? (This could include A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications)

These details will help me give you a definitive answer about your eligibility.

Based on the situation profile provided, I now have sufficient information to make an eligibility determination. Let me analyze Alex's case against the Child Benefit rules:

**Analysis for Alex:**

According to the rules:
- You normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and live in the UK
- **However**, you'll normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training
- Alex is 19 years old and is in approved education
- Alex lives with you (so you are responsible for the child)
- You live in the UK
- Alex is not in local authority care, hospital, or residential accommodation
- Alex does not work 24+ hours per week
- Alex has not started an apprenticeship in England
- Alex does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

Since Alex is 19 (under 20), lives with you, is in approved education, and none of the disqualifying factors apply, you meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit for Alex.

## Good News!

**You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Why you're eligible:

Although Alex is 19 years old (over the usual 16-year age limit), the rules allow you to continue claiming Child Benefit for children under 20 who remain in approved education or training. Since Alex:
- Is under 20 years old
- Lives with you in the UK
- Is in approved education
- Does not work 24+ hours per week
- Has not started an apprenticeship
- Does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

You meet all the requirements for Child Benefit.

### Important things to remember:

- Your Child Benefit will stop when Alex turns 20, or if they leave approved education before then
- If Alex starts working 24+ hours per week, starts an apprenticeship in England, or begins claiming certain benefits, your Child Benefit will stop
- If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit through the government website. If you have any other questions, feel free to ask!
